title: ALPR search activity compliance & audit records (SOP 205.5.1)
summary:
Asks for the audit records SOP 205.5.1 describes for individual ALPR search activity — operator usage, sign-on information, access dates and times, search-information entry, case-number compliance, and justification linkage.

Distinct in scope from the sharing-configuration audit memos produced under W012129-020926 and W012461-040226.

policy_promises.quote: audits must review operator usage and sign-on information; dates and times of access; entry of required search information by the End-User (case number, etc); and connection between searched data and listed justification
policy_promises.tests: What records address these specific search-activity audit criteria?

prior_pra_refs.note: W012129 produced sharing-configuration audit memos; this request addresses the separate search-activity audits described in SOP 205.5.1.

filed_because: SOP 205.5.1 describes quarterly audits that review individual searches' justification and case-number compliance. The request asks for records of those audits.
notes:
Initial partial denial (2026-03-17) cited Civil Code §1798.90.55(b), Gov. Code §7923.600, and §7927.705.

The request scope is for aggregate compliance metadata (whether required fields were populated) rather than search-result content.

2026-05-20 response split the disposition: Items 1(a) and 2(a) now produced on a rolling basis under W012541-041426; Items 2(b)-(c) and 3(b) declined as records that do not exist; Item 3(a) withheld as §7923.600 investigatory records; Items 2(d)-(e) under rolling email review.

2026-06-02 rolling update reports no responsive records located yet for Items 2(d)-(e); next update promised by 2026-06-16.

2026-06-16 rolling update (Juliana Santiago): another batch released; next update no later than 2026-06-30. New records include ALPR audit files and an internal 'Reason Entry Memo — Feedback requested ASAP' email thread plus an 'ALPR Update Memo — Reason Entry' — internal SMPD communications about reason/justification-field entry, responsive to the Item 2(d)-(e) non-compliance / corrective-action scope. The requester's 2026-06-16 reply asked the Department to specify which email corpus is being searched for Items 2(d)-(e).

2026-06-30, 2026-07-14, and 2026-07-28 rolling updates (Juliana Santiago, Management Analyst): three consecutive responses stating "a good faith and diligent search yielded no records responsive to your request" while keeping the request in rolling production, with the promised update pushed each cycle.

2026-08-11 response (Jennifer Maravillas, Captain-Support Services — first response on this request from the Support Services Captain, the officer SOP 205.5.1 designates to receive audit results): a new batch was released, reversing the three prior "no responsive records" statements; next update no later than 2026-08-25. The batch includes "Re: Question," a January 2026 email thread between Lt. Steve Casazza and Flock Customer Success Manager Tiffani Scates. Casazza writes that while "conducting a monthly audit of our network sharing" he found agencies "still just listing 'invest' or 'investigation' as their search reason with no offense code or case number although it says it is required," and asks whether that is a system glitch or whether officers can override the requirement. Flock replies 2026-01-08 that the behavior is "mostly tied to older versions of the Flock mobile app," whose "builds don't consistently enforce the offense type field," so "some searches are still coming through with 'investigation' only and no offense code or case number"; Flock states a mandatory mobile app update would close the gap. This is a record of searches identified as non-compliant for missing justification — Item 2(d) scope — dated January 2026, produced after the Department stated on 2026-04-22 and again on 2026-06-30, 2026-07-14, and 2026-07-28 that no responsive records existed.
